correctness.rationale: A direct separable convex decomposition covers the full parameter range. Born probabilities and conditional energies follow from Pauli-trace identities; uniform signs make distinct linear/edge Walsh characters orthogonal. The exact variance is a nonnegative sum. On an odd cycle, multi-affinity in the squared equatorial axis lengths proves that an optimizer can be chosen at all 0/1 endpoints. Every configuration with a zero has cost at least h² and an explicit alternating path attains it. For the all-equatorial class the least cycle-adjacency eigenvalue −2 cos(pi/n) gives cost at least n J²[1−cos(pi/n)]/2, attained by a Fourier-mode twist. This proves all-axis global optimality and the exact crossover. Separate Pauli matrix calculations and deterministic bounded tests pass, but tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: A core challenge in measurement-assisted charging is uniformity of the battery energy conditional on a measurement branch. The result gives a sharp variance lower bound in a fully separable family under a physically interpretable restriction (nonadaptive product readout) rather than just nonachievability. The field-to-coupling threshold partitions the entire odd-cycle family into distinct optimal sensor geometries; the crossover scales as n^(−1/2), and a simple 3-site state exhibits a strictly positive exact floor. Its scope is carefully restricted to conditional expected energy and does not claim collision-protocol robustness or entanglement necessity.
